top_categories.workout_context: 50ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Curacavi. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 78 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Curacavi's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Curacavi. Train it until it feels boring.
78 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
At Gran Fondo Curacavi, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Curacavi. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Base fitness for Gran Fondo Curacavi. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,937ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
